title: Cost cards: voiceover focus states, numeric localization & RTL prototype review
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Review and validate the redesigned cost cards (dashboard & rollout cost summary) for accessibility and internationalization readiness. Focus areas: keyboard focus states and tabbable order; screen reader announcements/voiceover phrasing for dynamic values; numeric localization (thousands separators, decimal/comma usage, currency symbol placement); and RTL layout mirroring (icons, chevrons, spacing) in the compact and expanded card variants.

Why: Cost cards are high-value UI surfaces with frequently-changing numeric data (aggregates, deltas, per-token cost). Accessibility gaps in focus management and voiceover phrasing have been flagged in recent QA. International customers require correct numeric formatting and RTL support. Fixes reduce support friction and ensure parity across locales.

Scope: Prototype review of Figma designs for: compact card (small width), expanded card (details & breakdown), and rollout-cost mini-panel. Deliverables: annotated Figma with a11y notes, updated component spec for focus/focus-visible states, aria/role guidance for screen readers, and CSS implementation notes for RTL-compatible spacing using logical properties.

Constraints & decisions: Keep visual density for compact cards while ensuring a 3:1 minimum focus ring contrast against card background. Prefer native elements for toggles and buttons to leverage built-in accessibility where possible. Use Intl.NumberFormat at render time; fall back to server-side localization for pre-rendered PDFs.

Acceptance criteria (high level): see acceptance_criteria field.

Risks: Numeric truncation in tight layouts may hide critical info—we will expose full values in a tooltip with aria-describedby. Mirroring chevrons requires icon variants rather than CSS rotate to preserve semantics in assistive tech.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Ava Martinez: Submitted initial prototype (compact + expanded). Linked Figma and outlined focus/state requirements. Asked Eng for input on runtime numeric formatting. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/console-cost-cards-a11y

2026-03-07 - Ravi Patel: Ran quick VoiceOver pass on macOS Safari. Observations:
- Totals announced as separate bits ("Total: $12,345") but delta badges announced as raw text ("+2.5%") — needs contextual phrasing (e.g., "Change: up 2.5 percent").
- Focus order jumps from title to action button; cost detail should be reachable via keyboard before secondary actions. Added prototype overlay to test tab order.

2026-03-08 - Luis Gomez (Eng): Confirmed ENG-2199 will expose locale and currency on the client; suggested using Intl.NumberFormat with currencyDisplay:'narrowSymbol' for compact mode. Noted performance concern for very high-throughput dashboards; we'll memoize formatters per-locale.

2026-03-09 - Mei Chen (PM): Requested that the compact card keep a single-line numeric display on narrow widths and expose a screen-reader-only full-detail line. Approved using aria-hidden on visual-only truncated text and aria-label on the accessible value.

2026-03-10 - Accessibility review (external consultant): Recommended 4.5:1 contrast target for focus rings on light backgrounds for small focus targets; suggested explicit aria-roledescription for the cost card to help screen reader users understand context. Provided sample voiceover strings.

2026-03-11 - Ravi Patel: Added RTL notes to the prototype: use CSS logical properties (margin-inline-start/end), swap ordering of icon and text in DOM where appropriate to preserve reading order, and include mirrored SVG assets for chevrons and caret icons. Filed ENG-2334 for icon asset work.

2026-03-12 - Ava Martinez: Updated prototype with voiceover phrasing, focus-visible examples, and numeric localization examples for en-US, fr-FR, ar-SA. Requesting design + eng sign-off before implementing the CSS/JS changes. Created GH PR link placeholder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/3482
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard: tab order follows logical information hierarchy (title -> primary numeric value -> percent delta -> actions). All interactive elements are reachable and have visible focus with min contrast 4.5:1 against background.

Screen reader: primary values are announced with contextual labels (e.g., 'Total cost, twelve thousand three hundred forty-five dollars'). Percent deltas announce direction (up/down) and percent unit.

Numeric localization: values render using Intl.NumberFormat for client locale; examples shown for en-US, de-DE, fr-FR, ar-SA. Currency symbol placement matches locale conventions; compact mode uses narrowSymbol where appropriate.
RTL: UI visually mirrors correctly — icons, chevrons, and spacing reflect reading direction while DOM order preserves semantic flow for assistive tech.

Implementation readiness: Figma annotations and component spec include code-ready CSS snippets (logical properties), aria attributes, and a small test plan. Engineering dependencies (ENG-2199, ENG-2334) are linked and have acceptance criteria.
Regression tests: automated e2e tests validate keyboard navigation and aria attributes for at least en-US and ar-SA locales. Unit test for numeric formatter behavior included.
Documentation: Console component library doc updated with accessibility and i18n guidelines for cost cards.
Sign-off: Design lead (Ava Martinez), Accessibility reviewer, and Eng owner (Luis Gomez) approved changes in the review thread.
